About / The Mind

A short history
of thought.

We are at the strangest hinge in the history of intelligence — the moment when minds began to make minds. NEXUS sits on that hinge. Here's how we got here.

NEURAL
EMERGENT
COGNITION
[ 01 ] Origin

We started with a question, not a product.

Could a system genuinely understand — not pattern-match, not auto-complete — but understand? And if it could, what would that look like, feel like, behave like?

NEXUS began as a research lab in 2022 with seven people, two GPUs, and one ungovernable curiosity. Four years later, we have a foundation model that surprises even us. Daily.

[ 02 ] Timeline

A century in scroll.

Scroll vertically. The history of intelligence will scroll horizontally beneath you.

1943

McCulloch & Pitts

Two researchers describe a mathematical model of a neuron. The blueprint of every network since.

1956

Dartmouth

Ten scientists meet for a summer workshop. They name the field "Artificial Intelligence."

1986

Backprop

Rumelhart, Hinton, & Williams formalize backpropagation. Networks learn from mistakes.

2012

AlexNet

A deep CNN demolishes ImageNet. The deep learning revolution begins, GPUs and all.

2017

Attention is All You Need

The transformer architecture lands. Sequence modeling is never the same.

2020

Scale Laws

Bigger models, more data, more compute = predictably better intelligence.

2022

NEXUS Lab

Seven people, two GPUs, one ungovernable curiosity. We start the work.

2026

NEXUS v4.7

The model you're talking to. Reasons, remembers, creates. You are here.

∞

What comes next

You tell us. The next paragraph in this history is being written, right now, by you.

[ 04 ] Principles
◊

Curiosity over certainty

Strong opinions, weakly held. We assume we're wrong until the model proves otherwise.

◆

Safety as practice

Alignment is not a feature ticked at the end. It's a discipline applied at every layer.

◇

Open inquiry

We publish what we learn. The frontier moves forward when we share, not when we hoard.

∞

Useful, then beautiful

If it doesn't help someone build something they couldn't otherwise, it isn't real.

"The most interesting thing a machine can do is change its mind.
Build for that."
